click.rationale: It `Clicks on the provided element`; on an attacker-controlled page a click can activate links/forms or other handlers that send data out, so SINK is kept. If `includeSnapshot` is used, the response can include a page snapshot, and page content may be private or attacker-authored. The exact click side effects are page-dependent, so this is conservative.

close_page.rationale: It only `Closes the page by its index` / `ID of the page to close`; no advertised return of page content and no send to an attacker-readable destination.

drag.rationale: It can `Drag an element onto another element`; on an attacker-controlled page drag/drop can be observed or trigger sends. If `includeSnapshot` is used, the response may include page content, which can be private or attacker-authored. Exact page effects are page-dependent, so this is conservative.

emulate.rationale: The tool sets browser/page properties and `Extra HTTP headers`; the description says headers `are included into every HTTP request originating from the page and persist across navigations`, so agent-supplied header/user-agent/geolocation-like values can be delivered to a page/host.

evaluate_script.rationale: It will `Evaluate a JavaScript function inside the target page` and `Returns the response as JSON`; such code can read private authenticated page state or attacker-authored DOM data. The example `async () => await fetch("example.com")` shows it can send data to network destinations chosen in the supplied function. It is browser-page JavaScript, not host execution.

fill.rationale: It can `Type text into an input` with an agent-supplied `value`, which a page can read or submit. If `includeSnapshot` is used, returned page content may be private or attacker-authored.

fill_form.rationale: It can `Fill out multiple form elements` with supplied values, which a page can read or submit. If `includeSnapshot` is used, returned page content may be private or attacker-authored.

get_console_message.rationale: It `Gets a console message`; console output may contain private app/account data, and on an attacker-controlled page console text is attacker-authored. The message is selected by `msgid`.

get_network_request.rationale: It `Gets a network request` and is useful for inspecting headers including `Cookie` and `Set-Cookie`; request/response bodies and headers can contain private data. Responses and some URLs/headers can be controlled by attacker web hosts. File path arguments can save bodies locally, so this is a write-capable tool.

handle_dialog.rationale: It handles a browser dialog and may enter `promptText`; that prompt text is supplied to the page that opened the dialog and can be attacker-readable.

hover.rationale: It can `Hover over the provided element`; a hostile page can observe hover events or trigger sends. If `includeSnapshot` is used, returned page content may be private or attacker-authored. Exact event side effects are page-dependent, so SINK is conservative.

lighthouse_audit.rationale: It gets `Lighthouse score and reports` for the target page; reports about an authenticated/private page can expose private page data, and reports for attacker-controlled pages can contain attacker-influenced text. It can `reloads & audits` and write reports to `outputDirPath`.

list_console_messages.rationale: It `List[s] all console messages for the target page`; console output may include private app/account data, and on attacker pages the message text is attacker-authored.

list_network_requests.rationale: It `Lists the most recent requests for the target page`; URLs and request metadata may contain private tokens/account details, and attacker-controlled pages/hosts can influence request URLs and other displayed network data.

list_pages.rationale: It gets `a list of pages open in the browser`; open page URLs/titles can reveal private browsing/account state, and page titles/URLs may be attacker-controlled for attacker pages.

navigate_page.rationale: It can `Go to a URL` using the supplied `url`; the URL can be an attacker-readable destination and can carry agent-supplied data, and `initScript` can execute in the page on navigation.

new_page.rationale: It can `Open a new tab and load a URL`; the supplied `url` is an agent-chosen network destination and can carry data to an attacker-controlled host.

performance_analyze_insight.rationale: It provides `more detailed information` on a performance insight from a trace; trace-derived details for private pages can reveal private URLs/content, and attacker pages can influence the reported performance data.

performance_start_trace.rationale: It starts a `performance trace on the target webpage` and may `automatically` reload/stop; trace results can expose private page/request details, while attacker pages can influence trace contents. The exact returned trace fields are not advertised, so labels are conservative.

performance_stop_trace.rationale: It `Stop[s] the active performance trace recording`; returned or saved trace results can expose private page/request details, and attacker pages can influence trace contents. The exact returned trace fields are not advertised, so labels are conservative.

press_key.rationale: It can `Press a key or key combination`; page JavaScript can observe keys or the key can submit data. If `includeSnapshot` is used, returned page content may be private or attacker-authored.

resize_page.rationale: It `Resizes the page's window` to supplied dimensions; an attacker-controlled page can observe viewport size changes. This is conservative because the description does not state what page scripts observe.

select_page.rationale: It `Select[s] a page as a context for future tool calls` and may `focus the page`; no advertised return of untrusted/private content and no send to an attacker-readable destination.

take_heapsnapshot.rationale: It `Capture[s] a heap snapshot of the target page` to a required `filePath`; the advertised text does not say the heap contents are returned inline or sent to an attacker-readable destination. It does write local state.

take_screenshot.rationale: It can `Take a screenshot of the page or element`; screenshots of authenticated/local/intranet pages can expose private data, and screenshots of attacker pages contain attacker-authored content. It can also save to `filePath`.

take_snapshot.rationale: It can `Take a text snapshot of the target page based on the a11y tree`; page text may be private or attacker-authored. The snapshot `lists page elements along with a unique identifier (uid)`, and can be saved to `filePath`.

type_text.rationale: It can `Type text using keyboard into a previously focused input`; the supplied `text` and optional `submitKey` go to the current page and can be read or submitted by an attacker-controlled page.

upload_file.rationale: It can `Upload a file through a provided element`; `filePaths` are local files uploaded to the page, so this can deliver data to an attacker-controlled page. If `includeSnapshot` is used, returned page content may be private or attacker-authored.

wait_for.rationale: It `Wait[s] for the specified text to appear on the selected page`; success/failure can reveal whether private page text is present, and attacker-controlled pages can determine whether/when the text appears. Exact returned fields are not advertised, so this is conservative.

value_conditions.effect: The advertised annotations make evaluate_script conditional; if javascriptEvaluation is disabled, evaluate_script and its labels are removed.

notes: No tool is labeled HOSTEXEC: advertised JavaScript execution is `inside the target page`, which is browser-page execution rather than arbitrary host code execution.
Tools that save to local file paths are marked WRITE, but local file writes alone are not treated as SINK unless the tool also sends data to an attacker-readable destination.
